facts.text: De Pijp means "The Pipe" and likely refers to its long, narrow streets that funnel people toward central Amsterdam.
The neighborhood grew around the Heineken Brewery, founded in 1864, whose brewing scent lingered until production stopped in 1988.
De Pijp's streets are named after Dutch painters such as Jan Steen, Frans Hals, Ruysdael and Vincent van Gogh, reflecting its artistic heritage.
The 2018 opening of De Pijp metro station beneath Ferdinand Bolstraat shifted commuters from trams to the underground, boosting citywide public transport use by 4%.
The area was once farmland outside Amsterdam’s medieval borders; rapid expansion in the 1870s brought industrial workers and shaped its working‑class character.
